findings.issue: The record stores replayCode, the hand's full 128-bit deck seed. shuffledDeck(replayCode) rebuilds the whole deck, so every bot's mucked or folded hole cards (and any undealt cards) can be derived from the stored record. That contradicts spec §8 and docs/storage/hand-records.md, which say the record 'never stores bots' unshown hole cards'. TASK-3.1 deliberately kept the replay code out of the DOM. REQ-052.2 requires the code, the record is written only after the hand ends, the data is local to the user's own origin, and the live code is already in memory, so there is no exploitable path today. It is a trap for future review/stats screens.
findings.evidence: IndexedDB hands record (DevTools, or a future screen reading HandStore.get) -> record.replayCode -> shuffledDeck(code) (src/engine/deck.ts:41) -> all seats' hole cards, including mucked hands
findings.fix: Correct the wording in spec §8 and docs/storage/hand-records.md: unshown cards are not stored as cards, but they can be derived from replayCode. Add a rule in the docs that a screen reading records must show only userHoleCards, shown and result.showdown, and must never deal from a stored replayCode for display. No code change is needed now.

findings.issue: parseHandRecord checks each field's type and range, and it never iterates keys or merges objects, so there is no prototype-pollution path. It does not check consistency across fields: action, showdown and award seats might not be in seats; cards might repeat (for example userHoleCards [5,5], or the board overlapping the hole cards); level is not checked against gameType; and seat names and the actions/awards arrays have no length limit. A record edited in DevTools could therefore pass validation and still be self-inconsistent. Today nothing renders or computes from records read back, so there is no reachable sink.
findings.evidence: DevTools-edited IndexedDB value -> HandStore.get -> parseHandRecord accepts -> (future) stats/review consumer
findings.fix: Add these checks when the first consumer of stored records arrives (TASK-3.10 or the stats/review screens): seat membership, distinct cards, and level null iff cash. Also put a sane cap on name length and array sizes.

summary: No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings. fake-indexeddb 6.2.8 is an exact-pinned devDependency, marked dev:true in the lockfile, with no runtime dependencies and no install scripts. It is imported only under tests/, and the headless lint bans it in src. npm audit reports 0 vulnerabilities. The session id comes from crypto.getRandomValues (16 bytes, CSPRNG). The record's explicit card fields hold only the user's hole cards plus showdownOf/result.showdown, which leave out mucked hands. Bots' hidden cards can still be derived from replayCode (MINOR, see the finding). HandStore exposes only add/get/count, add fails on a duplicate key, and there is no put or delete path. get always runs parseHandRecord, which fails closed with a RangeError naming only the field, not the value. console.error logs only the IndexedDB DOMException. The failure/delay test seams live only in e2e/support and are not reachable from src.
